q: A ____ capacitor is the simplest capacitor.
e: A parallel-plate capacitor is the simplest capacitor. Parallel-plate C grows with area and dielectric constant and falls when the gap grows. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum.

q: A parallel-plate capacitor consists of two parallel metal plates separated by air or other ____ material.
e: A parallel-plate capacitor consists of two parallel metal plates separated by air or other insulating material. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part.

q: The surface charge density on each plate is defined as charge per unit surface ____.
e: The surface charge density on each plate is defined as charge per unit surface area. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates. On each plate is defined as charge per unit surface ____. area.

q: If the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor are very close together, the electric field between the plates is ____.
e: If the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor are very close together, the electric field between the plates is uniform. Parallel-plate C grows with area and dielectric constant and falls when the gap grows. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum.

q: Because the electric field between the plates is uniform, the magnitude of the potential difference V between the plates equals ____.
e: Because the electric field between the plates is uniform, the magnitude of the potential difference V between the plates equals Ed. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current. Magnitude of the potential difference V between the plates equals ____. Ed.

q: For a given insulating material the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is directly proportional to the ____ of its plates.
e: For a given insulating material the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is directly proportional to the area of its plates. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add. Parallel-plate C grows with area and dielectric constant and falls when the gap grows.

q: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is inversely proportional to the ____ of the plates.
e: The capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor is inversely proportional to the separation of the plates. Parallel capacitors share voltage, charges add, and equivalent C is the sum. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: The permittivity $\epsilon$ of an insulating material is related to that of a vacuum $\epsilon_0$ as $\epsilon = K$ ____.
e: The permittivity epsilon of an insulating material is related to that of a vacuum epsilon0 as epsilon = K epsilon0. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum.

q: Here K is the ____ constant or the relative permittivity of the insulating material.
e: Here K is the dielectric constant or the relative permittivity of the insulating material. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part.

q: The permittivity of vacuum $\epsilon_0$ is approximately ____ $C^2 N^{-1} m^{-2}$.
e: The permittivity of vacuum epsilon0 is approximately 8.85 × 10^-12 C^2 N^-1 m^-2. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum. The power 10^-12 is the conversion for this unit; a nearby prefix is a different size.

q: For a vacuum K=____ and for other insulating materials K>1.
e: For a vacuum K=1 and for other insulating materials K>1. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part. The relation in this line is K=____ and for other insulating materials.

q: The dielectric constant of an insulating material is the ratio of its permittivity to that of ____.
e: The dielectric constant of an insulating material is the ratio of its permittivity to that of vacuum. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. Permittivity says how easily a material supports an electric field compared with vacuum.

q: The ratio of the capacitance with an insulating material to the capacitance with a ____ between the conductors is called the dielectric constant.
e: The ratio of the capacitance with an insulating material to the capacitance with a vacuum between the conductors is called the dielectric constant. An insulator does not let charge flow freely, so it can separate conductors or protect a live part. A conductor lets charge drift when a potential difference is applied across it.

q: When a charged capacitor is disconnected from a battery and a dielectric is inserted, the potential difference is found to ____.
e: When a charged capacitor is disconnected from a battery and a dielectric is inserted, the potential difference is found to decrease. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand.

q: Since the charge Q of a disconnected capacitor does not change when a dielectric is inserted, it indicates that the capacitance ____.
e: Since the charge Q of a disconnected capacitor does not change when a dielectric is inserted, it indicates that the capacitance increases. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand.

q: Insulating materials have values of dielectric constant K greater than ____.
e: Insulating materials have values of dielectric constant K greater than unity. Dielectric constant is permittivity over ε0, or C with the material over C with vacuum. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand.

q: A dielectric provides an increase in ____, an increase in maximum operating voltage, and possible mechanical support.
e: A dielectric provides an increase in capacitance, an increase in maximum operating voltage, and possible mechanical support. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. Voltage is potential difference, energy per unit charge between two points.

q: A dielectric increases the maximum operating ____ of a capacitor even though the physical size doesn't change.
e: A dielectric increases the maximum operating voltage of a capacitor even though the physical size doesn't change. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. Two conductors and a dielectric hold opposite charge, so energy sits in the electric field.

q: The dielectric may be able to withstand a larger electric ____ between the plates than air.
e: The dielectric may be able to withstand a larger electric field between the plates than air. A dielectric polarizes between the plates, raising C and the voltage the gap can stand. To withstand a larger electric ____ between the plates than air. field.
